item.title: Lazarus AI raises $43M with QBE and State Farm Ventures participating
item.description: Boston-based Lazarus AI announced $43M in funding with participation from QBE, State Farm Ventures, Mucker Capital and others. Its document-processing, cybersecurity and legacy-modernization AI runs on customer infrastructure, a pitch aimed squarely at regulated carriers that want control of data and models.

item.title: i23, AI-native commercial broker, raises £4.9M seed
item.description: London-based i23 raised a £4.9M seed co-led by Four Cities Capital, with Outward VC and Seedcamp joining. It plans to build its agentic broking platform and acquire traditional brokerages to roll its automated workflows across their books.

item.title: Marrow raises $2M to let AI agents buy insurance compliantly
item.description: London startup Marrow raised a $2M pre-seed led by Insurtech Gateway for a mediation layer between insurers' underwriting systems and consumer AI assistants. It handles disclosures, vulnerability checks and audit trails so agent-led purchases meet UK Consumer Duty rules.

item.title: Vertafore launches Velocity Change Request Agent for MGAs
item.description: Vertafore made its Change Request Agent available in Surefyre. It compares renewal and endorsement applications with existing policy records and summarizes changes in plain language for underwriter approval. In internal testing it cut review time by 70% and errors by 98%.

item.title: Guidewire unveils platform approach to agentic insurance
item.description: Guidewire introduced a governed platform for deploying AI agents across underwriting and claims on top of its core apps. It includes an Agentic Framework with guardrails and cost tracking, and it follows the company's $1.7B deal for hyperexponential announced Oct 27.

item.title: PolicyMe's in-house AI copilot cuts complex life underwriting time 59%
item.description: Canadian insurtech PolicyMe launched an AI underwriting copilot that consolidates medical evidence, summarizes cases, suggests decisions and drafts customer explanations. Internal data shows a 59% cut in underwriter turnaround on complex cases, and humans still approve every output.
